messages:
Anya Patel: Heads up - spotted CVE-2026-0457 in `fastxml` (transitive dependency pulled in by our model-serving image). PoC shows an info-leak when a crafted X-Forwarded-* header is present. Need triage and patch plan.

Samir Khan: CVE writeup: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-0457  — short summary: parsing edge-case allows header reflection. No public exploit yet but trivial to weaponize in some configs. :eyes:

Kurt Müller: Is this reachable from Hosted API or only Dedicated/Private installs?

Anya Patel: Quick rundown from scans: Hosted is on model-gateway v1.3.1 which includes the upstream fix. Several Dedicated pools still running 1.2.x (legacy images) and a handful of Private customers are on 1.2.0 or older because they opted out of auto-updates. Exposure: medium (requires crafted header) but public-facing endpoints + non-sanitized reverse proxies push this to high. I recommend P1 for Dedicated/public Private, P2 for Hosted where already patched.

Liz Chen: SLA question: will the patch require restarts that could violate 99.9%?

Anya Patel: Patch replaces the parser binary and requires rolling restart of the gateway process. We can do zero-downtime style by canarying new image across pods, but each pod restart adds ~5-10s of increased p95 for in-flight requests.

Samir Khan: Proposal: Hosted: immediate canary tonight 00:00 UTC (10% -> 50% -> 100%). Dedicated: targeted high-exposure pools within 48h in off-peak maintenance windows; offer expedited patching for Enterprise-tier customers. Private: CSM outreach and provide hot-patch instructions / advisory. Also recommend embargoed disclosure until customers are patched.

CSM-Jordan: I can start drafting customer notices for Enterprise and Dedicated contacts. Need a list of affected Dedicated pools and Private installs.

Kurt Müller: Ops calc: we need an estimate of SLA impact. Rolling restarts across zones vs per-pool — can someone quantify expected % of requests affected?

Liz Chen: We should avoid global windows during peak hours. Who owns the update automation for Dedicated pools? @Samir

Samir Khan: I'll own the update plan and script. Draft canary pipeline snippet below — simple k8s canary for model-gateway:

```
kubectl set image deploy/model-gateway model-gateway=redwood/model-gateway:1.3.2-canary
kubectl rollout status deploy/model-gateway
watch -n 1 kubectl get pods -l app=model-gateway
```

Will add healthchecks and circuit-breaker thresholds. I'll post the pipeline in #eng-releases when ready.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for hosted-model-gateway on cluster-us-west at 1781002460

Anya Patel: :eyes: Monitor error rates, KV-cache invalidations, and any weird JSON responses. Add a small QA prompt set to regen tests against the canary. Also tag the patch with the CVE ID and affected image hashes.

Kurt Müller: I ran a quick sim — if we do per-pod rolling across zones with a 2m stagger, impact is ~0.01% of monthly requests at worst. I'll produce a short SLA impact note and attach numbers.

CSM-Jordan: Looping in account teams for 6 Dedicated customers that are public-facing. They want immediate remediation options.

Liz Chen: Decision summary for this thread: P1 for Dedicated + public Private customers, P2 for Hosted when already patched. Schedule: Hosted canary tonight 00:00 UTC; Dedicated targeted patches starting in 48h (off-peak per region); Private customer outreach immediate. I'll update the incident tracker and maintenance calendar.

Anya Patel: Thanks all. I'll open the CVE triage doc, set an embargoed disclosure window (7 days) unless we see active exploit reports, and post follow-ups (patch hashes, affected pool IDs). Keep updates short in this thread.
